features: sixty capped shafts in a field a quarter-mile across
the taster's board - which wells are sweet this season, chalked daily
the ring: mud-brick cells and hide awnings around the field
the pound, where teams are watered in shifts through the night
a Roadwarden post with two rooms and a strongbox
hazards: a fouled well is not always obvious until the teams refuse it
attributes.position: on the beacon line, 6 days (~115 miles) south of Bell Harrow
sensory: hide lids cracking in the heat
attributes.water: 60 shafts, 9 sweet at any given season, the rest brackish to foul; the lens is shallow and drops through the summer

name: Sixty Wells
summary: Six days out from Bell Harrow, the first and last honest water on the plain: a field of sixty shafts sunk through the crust to a brine lens that is only just drinkable, each capped with a stone collar and a hide lid to keep the sun off. Nine of the sixty are sweet, and which nine changes with the season, so a crossing pays a taster before it pays anything else. The station is a low ring of mud-brick and awning around the well field, and it smells of rope, wet stone and the sulphur that comes up with the water.
